When it is \([[if test="is(floor(mod(t0,1440)/60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@floor(mod(t0,1440)/60)@}:[[if test="is(mod(mod(t0,1440),60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@mod(mod(t0,1440),60)@}\) [[if test="gw"]]GMT[[else]]local time in Nairobi (take Nairobi to be on \(37^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\))[[/if]], the local time on a ship is \([[if test="is(floor(mod(ts,1440)/60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@floor(mod(ts,1440)/60)@}:[[if test="is(mod(mod(ts,1440),60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@mod(mod(ts,1440),60)@}\). Find the ship's longitude.

[[input:ans1]] \(^\circ\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text: The ship's clock is [[if test="ahead"]]ahead[[else]]behind[[/if]] by \({@abs(dt)@}\) minutes. Each degree of longitude is \(4\) minutes of time, so the ship is \({@abs(dt)@} \div 4 = {@abs(dt)/4@}^\circ\) [[if test="ahead"]]east[[else]]west[[/if]] of [[if test="gw"]]Greenwich[[else]]Nairobi[[/if]].[[if test="gw"]][[else]] Nairobi is at \(37^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\), so the ship is at \(37^\circ [[if test="ahead"]]+[[else]]-[[/if]] {@abs(dt)/4@}^\circ\).[[/if]] The ship's longitude is \({@lon1@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="e1"]]E[[else]]W[[/if]]}\).

questiondescription.text:
Navigation: longitude from a time difference

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.7 (d) / Essential 2.3 (c): Find a ship's longitude from the difference between its local time and the time at Greenwich or Nairobi.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="gw"]]

The size is right, but check E or W. The ship's clock is [[if test="ahead"]]ahead of[[else]]behind[[/if]] GMT, and places to the east meet the sun first, so their clocks are ahead.

[[else]]

The size is right, but check E or W. The ship is \({@abs(dt)/4@}^\circ\) [[if test="ahead"]]east[[else]]west[[/if]] of Nairobi, and Nairobi is \(37^\circ\) east of Greenwich. Which side of the Greenwich meridian does that leave the ship?

[[/if]]
\(1^\circ\) of longitude is \(4\) minutes of time; divide the minutes by \(4\), not \(15\).
That is how far the ship is [[if test="ahead"]]east[[else]]west[[/if]] of Nairobi, not its longitude. Longitude is measured from the Greenwich meridian, and Nairobi is at \(37^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\).

You went \({@abs(dt)/4@}^\circ\) the wrong way from Nairobi. The ship's time is [[if test="ahead"]]ahead of Nairobi's, so the ship is east of Nairobi[[else]]behind Nairobi's, so the ship is west of Nairobi[[/if]].

falsefeedback.text: Your longitude would put the ship's clock [[if test="is(yt=0)"]]at the same time as[[else]]\({@abs(yt)@}\) minutes [[if test="is(yt>0)"]]ahead of[[else]]behind[[/if]][[/if]] [[if test="gw"]]GMT[[else]]the time in Nairobi[[/if]]. Compare that with the two times in the question. Each degree of longitude is \(4\) minutes of time: ahead means east, behind means west.
